editorial_examples.german: Tom brachte einen Toast auf Maria aus.

editorial_examples.german: Sie setzte die neue SIM-Karte in ihr Handy ein.
editorial_examples.english: She inserted the new SIM card into her phone.
editorial_examples.note: The candidate used the unrelated sense einsetzen meaning “begin/set in” and centered on rigor mortis. Replaced it with a clear, everyday insertion example.

editorial_examples.german: Lasst uns hier doch ein paar Kakibäume pflanzen!
editorial_examples.english: Why don’t we plant a few persimmon trees here?
editorial_examples.note: Corrected the outdated spelling Laßt to the current standard Lasst and refreshed the translation.

editorial_examples.english: The accepted proposal was put into practice.
editorial_examples.note: The source used akzeptiert as a finite verb form rather than illustrating the adjective entry. Replaced it with attributive adjective use.

editorial_examples.german: Er ist bei den älteren Bürgern sehr beliebt.
editorial_examples.english: He is very popular among older residents.
editorial_examples.note: The source translation used “it” for the masculine German pronoun Er and an unnecessarily mismatched subject.

editorial_examples.german: Der Zug fährt nur bis Frankfurt und kehrt dort.
editorial_examples.english: The train only goes as far as Frankfurt and turns back there.
editorial_examples.note: The candidate used the separable compound umkehren. Replaced it with a direct intransitive use of kehren meaning to return/change direction, attested by Duden.

editorial_examples.german: Die verteilten Unterlagen lagen auf dem Tisch.
editorial_examples.english: The distributed documents were on the table.
editorial_examples.note: The candidate used verteilt in a passive verb phrase, while this entry is the adjective. Replaced it with attributive adjective use.

editorial_examples.german: Wenn du Journalist sein willst, musst du aufmerksam sein.
editorial_examples.english: If you want to be a journalist, you have to be observant.
editorial_examples.note: Replaced the outdated gender-specific English “newspaperman” with a direct translation of the gender-neutral German Journalist.

editorial_examples.german: Er verkehrte in den besten Kreisen der Stadt.
editorial_examples.english: He moved in the city’s most elite circles.
editorial_examples.note: The candidate used verkehrt as an adverb meaning backwards; this entry is the verb verkehren. Replaced it with the verb meaning to socialize in a sphere.

editorial_examples.english: The metal parts must be grounded.
